hed: Treasury adds Iran-related sanctions on Russia’s VTB Bank
dek: The U.S. Treasury’s OFAC on Monday designated Russia’s VTB Bank Public Joint Stock Company under Executive Order 13902 for alleged Iranian sanctions evasion — including correspondent ties with sanctioned Iranian banks, offices in Iran, a rial–ruble settlement channel, and steps to move frozen Iranian assets — as part of Operation Economic Outcast. VTB was already under U.S. Russia-related sanctions from 2022 and 2025; Treasury said the Iran designation makes it among the world’s most comprehensively sanctioned lenders and raises secondary-sanctions risk for foreign institutions that keep dealing with it.

byline: Event summary from public reporting and named outlets

cl.body: Reuters’ Monday Washington wrap, CNBC’s Bessent write-through, and CNN’s Politics report stress that VTB was already cut off from the dollar system over Ukraine — so the new Iran designation is incremental (Treasury cites tens of millions blocked) — while flagging secondary-sanctions exposure for foreign banks that stay linked to VTB and questions about how much extra bite the step adds versus China’s Iran-oil trade.

cr.body: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s Operation Economic Outcast release, the Wall Street Journal’s same-day sanctions story, and The National’s maximum-pressure write-up frame the VTB hit as the promised “large bank” action meant to isolate Iran’s financial enablers — warning foreign institutions (including those touching VTB’s China footprint) that continued dealings now carry heightened secondary-sanctions risk under the administration’s economic campaign against Tehran.
